chunks: And the ghusl is in seventeen places: the ghusl of the seventeenth night of the month of Ramadan, and the nineteenth night, and the twenty-first night, and the twenty-third night, and for the two Eids, and upon entering the two Sanctuaries, and upon donning the ihram, and the ghusl of ziyara, and the ghusl of entering the House, and the day of Tarwiya, and the day of Arafa, and the ghusl of the deceased, and the ghusl of the one who gave ghusl to a deceased person or shrouded him or touched him after he became cold, and the ghusl of Friday, and the ghusl of the eclipse — when the entire disc was eclipsed and the person did not know about it
And the ghusl of janaba is an obligation, and likewise the ghusl of menstruation, because al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: The ghusl of janaba and menstruation are one.
And every ghusl includes wudu at its beginning, except the ghusl of janaba, because it is an obligation, and when two obligations convene, the greater of them suffices for the lesser.

key_terms.الترويه: Tarwiya: the 8th of Dhul Hijja, the day before the standing at Arafa during Hajj
key_terms.الكسوف: Kusuf: solar or lunar eclipse, which requires ghusl if the person was unaware during it
key_terms.غسل الجنابة: Ghusl of janaba: the obligatory ritual bath after major ritual impurity (sexual discharge, etc.)
key_terms.موطن: Place/occasion (mawtin): the specific ritual situations requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: How many types of ghusl are there in Shia Islam and when is ghusl required?
ai.summary: This legal ruling enumerates the seventeen occasions requiring ritual bathing (ghusl) in Shia fiqh, as transmitted in al-Amali al-Saduq. The text distinguishes between obligatory ghusls — specifically the ghusl of janaba (major ritual impurity from sexual intercourse or discharge) and the ghusl of menstruation — and recommended (mustahabb) ghusls for specific religious occasions. A notable jurisprudential ruling is cited from Imam al-Sadiq (AS): the method of ghusl for janaba and hayd is identical, and the ghusl of janaba, being obligatory, subsumes the wudu, whereas other ghusls require preceding wudu. The principle that the greater obligation subsumes the lesser when two coincide reflects a core maxim of Islamic jurisprudence.
